pin.h: Supreme Court hears the petition of Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders today
pin.text: After the directions of 11 October, all eyes are on what the court asks about the police action and the revision of the voter list. The Registry has already listed more than 10 defects in the petition.

items.text: Scroll: protesters picked up from central Delhi on Sunday afternoon said they were beaten in the van, their phones were snatched, and they were taken to a community centre in Pandwala Khurd, Najafgarh, about 40 km away, and released at 11:30 pm. The allegations are the protesters'; Delhi Police's reply is not in the report.

Chief Justice Surya Kant said on Monday that the protests and restrictions are not his 'issue', but the Supreme Court's doors are open to all. He kept confidential the reason for the meeting with Kharge and Rahul Gandhi not happening.

BJP's side: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan called the opposition's march 'theatrics' and accused Congress of weakening institutions. Anurag Thakur called the 'vote theft' allegations baseless. Both statements are allegations.

The Supreme Court Registry listed more than 10 defects in the petition of Rahul Gandhi and others, including a clear copy of Kharge's ID card and a court-fee shortfall of more than Rs 200. According to sources.

On Sunday protesters were not allowed to gather near Shivaji Park in Mumbai, and leaders of Uddhav Thackeray's Shiv Sena were detained outside Shiv Sena Bhavan. There are reports of 80 to 100 in Pune and of restrictions at Azad Maidan in Goa as well.
The Keralam Assembly passed a resolution demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, according to Scroll.

Newslaundry, citing reports by The News Minute and Scroll: more than 20 journalists say they were detained and their equipment snatched or broken even after the Supreme Court's direction of 11 October. The police's side is not in the report.
